Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray shows a well-circumscribed nodule in the left lower lung zone (left lower lobe) with an associated linear opacity extending to the pleura, indicative of pleural retraction. This radiographic appearance is characteristic of an inflammatory myofibroblastic tumour (IMT), which often presents as a solitary, well-defined mass that can cause local fibrotic reactions like pleural tethering.
